label: O(1) page free list
mechanism: the shared global-KV page free list becomes a deque, so handing out a page is O(1) popleft instead of an O(len) list.pop(0) memmove over the 65,536-entry pool
hypothesis: kv.GlobalPool holds ONE shared free list of max_batch * num_pages page ids — 64 * 1024 = 65,536 at the canonical operating point (server.build_resident num_pages=1024, serve max_batch=64) — and kv.PagedKV.ensure_pages hands pages out with self.free.pop(0). CPython's list.pop(0) is O(len): it memmoves every remaining element down one slot, so each page costs a ~0.4 MB memmove, measured 7.7 us at that pool size (tests/t_pagefree arm c: 0.7/2.0/3.9/7.7/15.3 us at pool 8k/16k/32k/64k/128k against a flat 0.02 us for deque.popleft — the O(len) shape, confirmed, not inferred). A canonical cohort pops 38,720 pages: 64 sequences x 11 global layers x ceil(745/16) = 47 prefill pages = 33,088, plus one page per PAGE_SIZE=16 decode tokens over the 128-token cap = 5,632. Every one of those pops runs on the host thread INSIDE the prefill traversal (kv.PagedKV.append -> ensure_pages, called from model.attn_prefill's per-row state seeding) or inside the decode step (model.py:831 / graphrun.py:337). collections.deque.popleft() is O(1) and the structure is a FIFO either way — scheduler.release_states extends the tail, ensure_pages takes the head — so the page-id stream is IDENTICAL, hence every page table, every KV placement and every tensor value is bit-identical. ONE VARIABLE: three lines of kv.py (the GlobalPool free list, the PagedKV non-backed free list, and ensure_pages' pop(0) -> popleft()), plus the one t_graphrun assertion that compared the structure to a list. No kernel, no numeric path, no scheduling decision, no shape. WHY THIS AND NOT A KERNEL: the ranked surface after exp-0022 and exp-0023 is prefill-term-dominated and its two named device-work levers (the MoE epilogue, the materialized prefill score tensor) both landed; what remains in prefill per exp-0021's fit is a large flat + per-row HOST term, and this is the single largest identified O(n^2) contributor inside it. EVIDENCE, isolated (tests/t_pagefree, CPU only, pinned to a NUMA-0 core so it could run while the dispatcher held GPUs 4-7; log /workspace/logs/t_pagefree_exp0024_out.log): arm a ORDER — replaying the canonical cohort schedule against both structures gives 38,720 allocated page ids with elementwise-identical streams and identical final free lists, which is the correctness argument in full (the free list's only output is the page-id stream); arm b COST — 281.6 ms -> 3.4 ms per cohort, 82x. EVIDENCE, IN SITU on the real resident model, which is the arm exp-0018's post-mortem says was never run for a host-side deletion (tests/t_pagefree_insitu, GPUs 4-7, one resident load, 11 global pools at the full 65,536 free pages, canonical 6-row group at ISL 690-800, arms INTERLEAVED with the pools reset to full length before every rep so neither arm sees a drained list; log /workspace/logs/t_pagefree_insitu_exp0024_out.log): deque 736.6/735.8/735.7 ms host + 0.3 ms device tail, list 762.8/762.8/762.6 ms host + 0.3 ms device tail, MEDIAN 736.1 vs 763.1 ms = 27.0 ms per 6-row traversal (3.54%), repeats agreeing to 0.5 ms. The separation predicted from the isolated cost (3,102 pops x 7.7 us = 24 ms) lands within 3 ms of it, so the CUDA launch queue does NOT absorb the memmove: 27 ms of added host work buys 27 ms of added wall. That differential does not require settling whether the traversal is host- or device-bound overall (the open exp-0021 arm-b question, which exp-0023's spec answered from the utilization log) — it only says the traversal is host-limited AT THE MARGIN, which is exactly the condition under which deleting host work pays. SCALING NOTE, not part of the claim but the reason this is worth fixing rather than tolerating: the cost is O(max_batch * num_pages) per pop and the pop count is also proportional to max_batch, so it grows QUADRATICALLY with concurrency — at the frozen canonical concurrency 512 (ARCHITECTURE rev 4) the pool is 8x larger and the pop count 8x higher, i.e. ~64x this cost.
predicted_delta: +1.3 to +1.9% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 448-450 vs the accepted exp-0023 row 441.8 (merge bar 443.1). Cycle model from exp-0023's own ledger block (612 s, 2112 requests, 270,336 tokens): a 64-sequence cohort is 8192 tokens = 18.5 s, and the box holds ~33 of them. Per cohort the measured in-situ saving is 27.0 ms x (64/6) = 288 ms of prefill traversal, i.e. 1.56%, giving 448.7 tok/s. The decode-side pops (5,632 of the 38,720, 14.5%) are worth a further ~43 ms/cohort at the same 7.7 us, which would put it at 1.79% / 449.7, but I do not count on them: those pops sit in the graphed step's host-side pre-work, where the GPU may still be replaying the previous graph, and no arm measured them. FLOOR CASE: 288 ms/cohort is a directly measured wall-clock difference on the real engine through the real Scheduler, not an extrapolation from a microbenchmark, so the main way this reads null is if the canonical box forms far fewer full 6-row cohorts than exp-0017's admission logic implies — which would itself be worth knowing, and would show up as the saving scaling with traversal COUNT rather than sequence count. It cannot read negative: deque.popleft is strictly cheaper than list.pop(0) at every pool size measured, and nothing else changes.

local_pregate.tf_gate: NOT RUN, and deliberately so — the change is value-preserving BY CONSTRUCTION and t_pagefree arm a proves it directly: the free list's only output is the sequence of page ids ensure_pages appends to self.table, and that sequence is elementwise identical between the two structures over a full canonical cohort schedule (38,720 ids), as are the final free-list contents. Identical page tables mean identical KV placements mean identical gathered K/V mean identical tensors everywhere downstream, so no gate arm CAN move. This follows exp-0022's precedent of substituting a bitwise-equivalence arm for the local gate when the diff cannot reach the numerics. The budget also made it the right call: the dispatcher held GPUs 4-7 until 20:05 with its exp-0023 bench and the local gate is a ~22 min run after a ~102 s load, so the GPU window was spent on the in-situ arm, which is the arm that could actually have killed the experiment.
local_pregate.determinism: unchanged and unchangeable by this diff. The page-id stream is a pure function of the schedule under both structures (arm a), no tensor op is added or removed, and the graphed decode step's capture is untouched — ensure_pages runs on the host before replay, as it did. Two identical runs of the same schedule remain bitwise identical for exactly the reasons they were before.
local_pregate.algebra: arm a of tests/t_pagefree is the algebra: FIFO in, FIFO out. release_states appends at the tail (list.extend / deque.extend are the same operation), ensure_pages takes the head (list.pop(0) / deque.popleft return the same element), so the two structures are observationally equal and differ only in the cost of the head removal.
local_pregate.syntax: py_compile clean. engine/pyengine/kv.py +19/-7 (three functional lines plus comments), engine/pyengine/tests/t_graphrun.py 1 line (gp.free == list(...) -> list(gp.free) == list(...), needed because a deque never compares equal to a list), engine/pyengine/tests/t_pagefree.py and t_pagefree_insitu.py new. harness/, configs/, goldens/, ledger, prompts, loop scripts untouched. Sanity-run on this tree: t_graphrun ALL OK (t_ctx_static, t_searchsorted_offs, t_scratch_pools), and a PagedKV built with an explicit free_order=[3,1,0,2,5,4,7,6] still allocates [3,1,0].
local_pregate.memory: strictly lower: a deque of 65,536 ints is the same element count in block-linked chunks instead of one contiguous pointer array, and no tensor allocation changes. Host-side only.
